title: Fitting singular subscheme of a nodal relative curve
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes. Assume every nonempty geometric fibre is equidimensional of dimension $1$ and has only ordinary double point singularities (equivalently, at a singular geometric point its completed local ring is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ for an algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$). Let $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\hookrightarrow X$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Then the relative smooth locus $U\subset X$ is open and the underlying set of $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$ is $X\setminus U$; $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\to S$ is unramified. For every morphism $S'\to S$, if $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ is the base change, then the first-Fitting singular subscheme of $f'$ is canonically $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\times_SS'$ and its underlying set is the nonsmooth locus of $f'$.

source.place: Tags 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family) and 0C5B (lemma-base-change-nodal-family), using Divisors Tags 0C3I (Fitting formation), 0C3J (zero-Fitting unramifiedness), and 0C3K (dth-Fitting smooth locus)

proof.text: For $g:S'\to S$ write $p:X'=X\times_SS'\to X$. Local finite presentation implies local finite type by forgetting relations in an affine finite presentation. Apply [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change]: $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ is finite-type quasi-coherent and $\Omega^1_{X'/S'}\cong p^*\Omega^1_{X/S}$. Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-pullback] with $r=1$ and $\mathcal F=\Omega^1_{X/S}$. Its equality of image ideals and its closed-stratum comparison, with [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], give the canonical equality $\operatorname{Sing}(f')=\operatorname{Sing}(f)\times_SS'$ over $X'$.

Apply [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] with $d=1$. Flatness, local finite presentation and pure dimension of every nonempty geometric fibre are the stated hypotheses. Its $Z_1$ is $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$ by [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], so $U$ is open and $|\operatorname{Sing}(f)|=|X|\setminus U$.

Put $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(f)$. Locally $Z\to S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $A$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra. The images of its finitely many algebra generators generate $A/I$, so $Z\to S$ is locally of finite type by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Step 1 identifies $Z_{\bar s}$ with $\operatorname{Sing}(C/\Omega)$ for $C=X_{\bar s}$. If $C$ is empty this morphism is unramified by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Otherwise clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $C$ locally finitely presented, hence locally of finite type. It is pure of dimension one and nodal by hypothesis; implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) of [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion] gives $Z_{\bar s}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ unramified. Now [lem-trf-geometric-fibre-unramified-criterion] gives $Z\to S$ unramified.

source.place: Tag 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family), via Tag 0C4E and Morphisms Tag 02G8

proof.text: After arbitrary $S'\to S$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] give flatness and local finite presentation of $f'$. For any $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S'$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $(X\times_SS')\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, using the composite $\bar t\to S$; both represent pairs of compatible maps to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Thus nonempty geometric fibres still have pure dimension one. Apply [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] to $f'$ with $d=1$ and combine its support equality with step 1. No reduction of a closed subscheme is taken.
